claims.text: Integrating high-throughput combinatorial sputtering with high-resolution local composition and phase mapping enables precise prediction of low-phonon-thermal-conductivity high-entropy alloys.
The integrated approach will improve prediction accuracy by at least 30% relative to bulk-average models.
Combinatorial sputtering can produce CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy films with continuous composition gradients under controlled conditions.
Improved EDS, XRD, and TEM can capture subtle nanoscale inhomogeneities relevant to thermal-conductivity prediction.
Rapid laser-flash measurements can provide spatially resolved thermal-conductivity data across combinatorial thin films.
Spatially resolved thermal, compositional, and phase data can be acquired from the films between room temperature and 500 K.
Local phase variations affect phonon scattering.
Subtle local compositional and phase variations act as phonon scatterers.
Bulk-average models overlook these local phonon-scattering features.
Adding locally resolved descriptors improves the predictive model's correlation with reduced thermal conductivity.
Regions selected by the predictive model will have measured thermal conductivity at least 30% below the values predicted by conventional bulk-average approaches.
The approach is expected to be effective primarily in thin-film systems where high-resolution spatial characterization is feasible.
The approach may have limited applicability to bulk samples and systems without measurable composition gradients.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis defines the claimed 30% benefit as improved prediction accuracy, whereas the predicted outcome defines it as measured conductivity being 30% lower than the baseline model's predicted value. A lower measured value relative to a prediction is not itself a 30% improvement in predictive accuracy.
